title: Add correlation keys, SLO-aware dashboards, and alert tuning after capacity regression
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Summary: During the 2026-03-08 capacity regression (INC-2026-03-08-01) the Console dashboards and tracing instrumentation did not provide the signal required by on-call to rapidly diagnose the root cause. Symptoms included: missing per-route queue_length metrics, absent KV cache hit-rate spans for model serving requests, dashboard panels broken out only at the service level (no customer/route cardinality), and alerts that fired on noise rather than sustained backpressure. Impact: 26 minutes of degraded request latency across the hosted API and two customer-facing SLO breaches. Root causes found in postmortem analysis: (1) several high-cardinality metrics were never instrumented due to concerns about metric cardinality and storage cost; (2) a tracing migration dropped a span in the request enqueue path; (3) alert thresholds were static and not SLO-aware; (4) runbooks referenced outdated dashboard names. Goal: deliver targeted observability additions, dashboard redesign, and alerting/playbook changes to eliminate these blind spots and reduce MTTD for similar events to under 5 minutes.
action_items: Instrument request-correlation: add a stable request_id header propagation through model-routing and worker queues. Owner: Ethan Zhang. Due: 2026-03-16. Status: in-progress (PR #1432).
Add queue and backlog metrics: expose per-worker queue_length and route_pending_requests (tagged by product_route and deployment_zone). Owner: Priya Rao. Due: 2026-03-18. Status: planned.
Restore missing spans: add an explicit 'enqueue' span around the scheduler handoff so traces show queue wait time. Owner: Marco Fuentes. Due: 2026-03-15. Status: in-review (trace PR #88).

Create SLO-aware dashboards: new Console dashboard template shows per-route p50/p90/p99 latency, queue_length heatmap, KV cache hit-rate, and request throughput with customer filter. Owner: UX Analytics (lead: Dana Liu). Due: 2026-03-19. Status: design accepted.

Tune alerting: replace static thresholds with anomaly windows and SLO burn-rate alerts; add minimum sustained window to reduce flapping. Owner: Observability SRE (lead: Aaron Klein). Due: 2026-03-20. Status: backlog.

Runbook updates: update the capacity incident runbook with links to new dashboard panels, triage checklist (check queue_length, cache hit-rate, per-route throttles), and escalation matrix. Owner: On-call Guild. Due: 2026-03-14. Status: in-progress.

Cost/Retention plan: propose metric cardinality controls (rollup, low-cardinality sampling and short-retention high-cardinality metrics) and estimate monthly cost. Owner: FinOps (liaison: Maya Patel). Due: 2026-03-22. Status: blocked (awaiting telemetry cost model).

Post-deploy verification: add automated dashboard smoke tests and a synthetic load that validates queue_length metrics and trace spans in staging. Owner: CI Reliability. Due: 2026-03-25. Status: planned.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Sofia Martinez: Created ticket after postmortem call. Attached incident timeline and rough impact numbers. Suggested prioritizing request correlation and enqueue span first to speed diagnosis in next event.

2026-03-11 - Aaron Klein: Observability SRE reviewed. Recommended SLO burn-rate alerts to prevent noisy thresholding. Noted that rollout should include feature flags for high-card metrics to control cost.
2026-03-11 - Ethan Zhang: Started instrumenting request_id propagation; implemented end-to-end header and added tests. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1432.

2026-03-12 - Marco Fuentes: Trace PR updated after review to ensure span tags include request_id and route. Current trace retention in staging verified. Follow-up: confirm sampling policy will keep enqueue spans at 100% for error/slo-breach traces.
2026-03-12 - Priya Rao: Queue metric design doc posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Queue+Metrics+Design. Need sign-off from FinOps before broad rollout.
2026-03-12 - Dana Liu: Dashboard mockups uploaded to Drive and Console UX review scheduled for 2026-03-13. Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/obs-dashboard-designs.
acceptance_criteria: New request_id header is propagated end-to-end and appears in logs/traces for 100% of non-sampled requests in staging.
Per-route queue_length and route_pending_requests metrics are present in production with tags product_route and deployment_zone and show sensible distributions under synthetic load.
Console has a SLO-aware dashboard template and at least two live dashboard instances: (1) global SRE view, (2) per-customer triage view.
Alerting rules replaced or augmented with SLO burn-rate and sustained-window checks; alert noise reduced in canary run.
Runbook updated and validated in a tabletop exercise with on-call team.
notes: Trade-offs considered: adding high-cardinality metrics vs cost. Temporary sampling and short retention windows are acceptable until FinOps approves long-term storage.
Blockers: telemetry billing model needed to finalize retention policy. FinOps action assigned (Maya Patel).
Related: ENG-13102 and ENG-15893 cover metric ingestion pipeline upgrades and missing tracepoint consolidation respectively. Coordinate rollout windows to avoid double instrumentation.
Expected MTTD improvement: from ~12 minutes in the incident to <5 minutes after changes.
